slides.title: System Calls
content: A system call is an interface that allows user programs to request services from the operating system kernel for tasks like file access, process control, and device communication
System calls switch execution from user mode to kernel mode to perform privileged operations safely
Categories include process control, file management, device management, information maintenance, and communication
They ensure security, hardware abstraction, and controlled resource management

slides.title: System Boot Process
content: The system boot process is the sequence of steps that initializes hardware and loads the operating system into memory after power-on
POST checks hardware components like CPU and RAM for errors
BIOS or UEFI identifies bootable devices and loads the bootloader
The bootloader loads the OS kernel, which initializes system services and prepares the system for user interaction

slides.title: Interrupts
content: Interrupts are signals that temporarily halt CPU execution to handle urgent events through an interrupt service routine :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}
Hardware interrupts are triggered by external devices like keyboards or disks and occur asynchronously
Software interrupts are generated by programs or errors and occur synchronously
Interrupts improve system responsiveness and efficiency by avoiding constant polling

slides.title: Event-Driven & Resource Management
content: Event-driven programming executes tasks based on events such as user input, interrupts, or system signals instead of sequential execution
It uses event loops and handlers to respond to events efficiently and asynchronously
Resource management ensures efficient allocation of CPU, memory, storage, and devices among processes :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
It focuses on fairness, efficiency, security, and optimal utilization of system resources

slides.title: Priority Inversion & Load Balancing
content: Priority inversion occurs when a high-priority process waits for a lower-priority process holding a shared resource
It can be solved using techniques like priority inheritance and priority ceiling protocols
Load balancing distributes tasks across multiple processors or systems to avoid overload
It improves performance, reduces response time, and ensures efficient resource utilization

slides.title: Performance Measurement & Tuning
content: Performance measurement involves analyzing metrics like CPU usage, memory usage, throughput, and response time
Performance tuning involves optimizing system parameters, applications, or hardware to improve efficiency
Tools like system monitors, profilers, and benchmarks help identify bottlenecks
Proper tuning enhances scalability, stability, and overall system performance
